title: Circulatory, Respiratory and Digestive Systems
seo_title: Grade 9 Natural Sciences: Circulatory, Respiratory and Digestive Systems Worksheets (CAPS)
standard_code: Grade 9 Natural Sciences: Circulatory and respiratory systems; digestive system
standard_text: The circulatory system (heart, blood vessels, blood) transports substances; the respiratory system takes in oxygen and removes carbon dioxide by gaseous exchange in the alveoli; the digestive system breaks food down into small molecules that are absorbed into the blood. (summary of CAPS Natural Sciences, Grade 9, Life and Living: Circulatory and respiratory systems; digestive system)
meta_desc: Free Grade 9 Natural Sciences worksheets (CAPS): the heart and blood vessels, blood, breathing and gaseous exchange, digestion and absorption. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: The heart pumps blood; the lungs exchange gases.
key_sub: Food is digested and absorbed in the small intestine.
body_html:
How to think about it

The heart pumps blood through arteries (away from the heart), capillaries and veins (back to the heart). Blood carries oxygen, food and wastes. In the lungs, oxygen diffuses from the alveoli into the blood and carbon dioxide diffuses out.

Digestion breaks food down: the mouth (teeth and saliva), oesophagus, stomach (acid and enzymes), small intestine (digestion and absorption through villi) and large intestine (water is absorbed). Enzymes speed up digestion.

Example

Which blood vessels carry blood away from the heart?

A for away

Answer: arteries

Example

Where are most nutrients absorbed?

A long tube with villi

Answer: the small intestine

Common mistakes

  • Thinking the lungs pump blood.
  • Thinking food is absorbed in the stomach.
  • Thinking veins carry only oxygen-poor blood (the pulmonary vein does not).

faq.q: Why does your breathing get faster when you exercise?
faq.a: Your muscles need more oxygen and produce more carbon dioxide.

faq.q: Why do the alveoli have thin walls?
faq.a: So that gases can diffuse across them quickly.

items.e: Breathing in: diaphragm and intercostals contract, ribs up and out, volume up, pressure down, air rushes in.

A sheet of muscle under the lungs that contracts and flattens when we breathe in.
items.e: Each part has a job.

items.q: Amylase in saliva breaks starch into sugars. Is this physical or chemical digestion?
items.e: Physical digestion breaks food into smaller pieces; chemical digestion uses enzymes to break large molecules into small ones.

items.q: What are the end products when starch (a carbohydrate) is digested?

items.q: Which food substance does protease digest?
items.e: Protease digests proteins.

items.e: Physical digestion breaks food into smaller pieces; chemical digestion uses enzymes to break large molecules into small ones.

items.q: Food enters the stomach. Which part did it come from?
